newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent spot products track NYMEX higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent spot products track NYMEX higher.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent spot unleaded gasoline and diesel fuel prices tracked a sharp rise in the NYMEX complex on Monday on steady differentials late in the day, traders said.

NYMEX January gasoline ended the day up 2.66 cents a gallon at a contract-high 68.12 cents, and front-month heating oil finished up 1.89 cents a gallon at 73.57 cents on supply concerns that rippled through the futures market.
The NYMEX gains boosted Midwest basis in what some had expected to be a slow trading day as players assessed positions heading into the final weeks of the year.

In addition to December deliveries, traders were focused on year-end accounting moves that were expected to fuel some activity in the weeks before the market loses liquidity ahead of the upcoming holidays.
"Today is a capture data day," one Chicago-area trader said. "I think you are going to have to make your moves this week or you may not be able to get them implemented."
High sulphur diesel was bid 1.50 cents a gallon under the print in Chicago and 2.0 cents under in Group Three on dormant agricultural demand, traders said.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was talked 0.75/1.0 cent a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and 0.75/0.50 cent a gallon under the print for later deliveries.
Group Three first-cycle low sulphur diesel was talked 0.50/0.75 cent a gallon over the print, with later deliveries 1.75/1.50 cent a gallon under the print.
